text:
mira: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime push I'm seeing a small but consistent p99 delta (~+2.3%) for short prompts on hosted models. Looks host-side: tokenization + streaming chunking spike. @jon can you eyeball the flame I uploaded? https://perf.redwood/trace/9387654321
jon: loading it now. rough question — is this only on HTTP/gRPC frontends or affects dedicated too?
mira: affected traffic is mainly hosted HTTP paths (edge proxy -> host). Dedicated canaries are clean, so routing + chunking probably in play.
kevin: two quick suspects: 1) kernel selection edge-case where small seqs are classified as wide-kernel, increasing kernel launch cost; 2) streaming chunk size decreased -> more writev/syscalls. both can raise host tail.
lina: saw similar in a local repro last week. the inline tokenization optimization changed the parse hot-path layout — fewer memcopies but more small syscalls when streaming is enabled.
perf-bot: perf-summary: host_parse=42%, syscalls(writev/send)=23%, kernel_select=13%, kv_cache_miss=6%, other=16% (sampled). link: https://perf.redwood/summary/9387654321
jon: can you paste the minimal repro curl? want to reproduce locally w/ --http2 and streaming.
mira: here — small streaming client that triggers the hotpath:
```
curl -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" "https://api.redwood/v1/stream?model=mantic-v2" --data-binary @- 
# send a bunch of 3-20 char prompts quickly
```
kevin: try toggling stream.chunk_threshold from 8 -> 64 in canary, and pin kernel selector to prefer narrow for seq < 64. quick experiment I ran reduced syscalls by ~35%.
lina: another quick check: toggle inline-tokenizer=true/false in host binary. when disabled I saw p99 drop but CPU microprofile shows more memcpy time (tradeoff).
sre-bot: Alert(inc): host-p99-increase model=mantic-v2 window=02:10-02:40Z delta=+2.3% severity=low. Investigating owners: @mira @jon
mira: ran canary with stream.chunk_threshold=64 and kernel pin narrow for short seqs. early metrics: p99 down ~1.8% vs broken prod, kv-cache spill rate up ~0.4% (still within tolerances). will open a rollback-protect PR that toggles both knobs behind flags.
jon: good. can you also collect eBPF syscall stack for a sample minute? i want stacks for writev/sendmsg to confirm top callers.
kevin: quick eBPF snippet i use:
```
sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_writev { @[comm] = count(); }' -d 60
```
mira: will run during next canary wave and attach logs.
perf-bot: archived trace + diff: https://perf.redwood/diff/9387654321?exp=kernelpin_vs_prod
lina: long term we should add a sequence-length histogram to kernel-selector and a streaming syscall rate alarm so we don't regress with small-chunk streaming changes.
mira: agree. created ticket infra#1427 to add hist + alarm. I'll post the rollback PR in ~30m. :thumbsup:
jon: once PR is up i'll run microbench across kernels and batching heuristics. thanks everyone.
